restrictions: Messages are exactly 135 bytes; each is one padded block M || 0x86 with zero capacity (520 fixed state bits). Complete fixed-zero-IV SHA3-256 sponge with suffix 0x06 and pad10*1, prefix rounds 0..4, 256-bit digest.

This package (v22) is our v20 (84668773) with the counted programs of proof X, which re-derive, adopt and extend the four tightenings of Th0rgal's v21 (a9ec6971, itself our v20; credited, co-author; its build checks D21 charged): match step 62 -> 56 per match + 3 per 16 matches of a run (Th0rgal's masked tail constants and carry-free byte fold, the 16-bit sum into the top field, the run loop unrolled 16 times; per_a 11 -> 18 inside the 2^6 sort-and-merge bound); T2 leaf with its Gray step 56 -> 26 (Th0rgal's identity for ALLOW as two lane selections, no redundant leaf counter, a state step for Knuth's Algorithm H); half-vector step 96 -> 83 (the same state step, with the entry pointer's advance); E block 69,242 -> 66,831 (Th0rgal's D2[0] registers, no per-step counter, the pass word formed only for stage 2; the prologue's stores and a spill now counted). algorithm() and everything it reaches are v20's byte for byte; R7 measures v22 (X.11).

v20's changes, kept (proof W): rule K (written and hashed before R7, no run outcome as input) fixes K = 50, A_ADV = 1067, A_MAX = 4268, S2CAP = 2^11; success is measured by R7, 48 pre-registered complete runs; C (whose only role was keeping K = 96) is not charged, G2 is; P's T3 runs core by core (memory under 2^28 bytes; the repair 0xshikhar published first in 6667fc4f and 395e8a28); D15's native runs are priced with their half vectors at every level; D20 charges every run made for v20 except the organizer's harness and R7. Everything else is v20's: X_MAX = 2^20, B_TRUE = 2^29 units, B_BUDGET, CCAP, B', S, connector, E's function, P's output, the certificates.

Considered and not adopted: B2 (proof X.7: a 31-primitive popcount filter plus an exact re-count of v15's stopped contiguous run). The re-count would fix a number of the claim, so our rule (every run we make is charged; v15 charged its own count-only recounts) charges it, and then B2 cannot lower the total: at least 33.1422 with the re-count charged (at least 32.8829 if it were left uncharged, which is not our rule); not run, not claimed. 395e8a28's T.1 and T.3 (W.11): with their runs charged neither lowers the total; not adopted.

No advice: the algorithm runs every phase itself; its time is the sum of caps, fixed counts and organizer-recomputed counts times counted prices or stated bounds (proof 2, 6, U, V, W, X): P 2^28.5281 units (T2 2^24.9066, T3 core by core, half vectors 2^21.5052, matches 2^24.6350); B' 2^29 units (B_TRUE) plus one update; at most A_MAX = 4268 connector attempts of at most X_MAX = 2^20 work units (2^28.5132); E: K = 50 spaces, setup at most 2^16 units, 2^16 unrolled blocks of 256 Gray steps at most 66,831 counted primitives each (2^27.2680), at most S2CAP = 2^11 stage-2 pairs per space (2^18.4559). Algorithm 2^30.4623.

Development (proof 0.1, U, V, W, X, H2): every target-specific run at the counted prices of the submitted programs: G2 2^30.9572, D15 2^32.0018, D16 2^27, D19 2^28.8303, D20 2^29.0748, D21 2^22.6078 (v21's build checks), D22 2^26.7962 (every run we made for v22 except the organizer's harness); C not charged (rule K). Total 2^33.093387, claimed 33.09339; preprocessing 2^33.004263, claimed 33.00427. Sensitivities, not claimed: no repricing of earlier development at v22's programs 33.1571; C charged 33.6128; R7 charged 33.9770; C, R5, R6 and R7 charged 35.5610; S2CAP at 2^21 33.1502; our local organizer runs charged 33.3294; D15 doubled 33.6485; v17's B' re-derivations charged 33.9101; A1 charged 40.9861.

History, stated plainly (W.1): rule K reads no run outcome, but it was written after G2, C, D, C', R5 and R6 had run, and its author knew their outcomes (R5 46/48 and R6 44/48 at K = 96; positive spaces per enumerated space 0.037 and 0.031, above the model's 0.0265; each 40/48 if truncated at 50 spaces; stage-2 maxima 308 and 315). The power level 0.999 and S2CAP's factor 8 were chosen with that knowledge, and v19 declined the rule for that reason. The knowledge did not lower any constant: under the model every conventional level gives a smaller K (0.95: 39, 0.99: 44), and the observed rates would give 36 or 43 even at 0.999. rule.txt, which states this history, and R7's plan were hashed together at 2026-10-08T15:23:01Z, before any R7 run; the charged sensitivities are printed above.

Premise P (inside H1; success only): P outputs the trail of proof 3 within M_CAP. P's native run certified it at its level of 64 blocks (W* = 127 <= 2 x 64 - 1, Lemma P: every leaf with AS(alpha2) <= 63 is found, every other leaf has w1 >= 128), with 7,251,935 matches; the organizer recomputes the structural counts, the output core's level (r5-count trial 10), seed-picked cores (r5-mitm-0, 1) and P's driver on a sub-problem with its cap. v20 runs T3 core by core with the same output (Lemma W). If P certified nothing it would output nothing; every cost bound holds either way.

Probability space: the algorithm's own coins (B' candidate coins, connector coins), fixed target, no advice. Success is measured end to end by R7 (proof W.2, Appendix F): rule K, plan, driver, analysis and every file hashed at 2026-10-08T15:23:01Z before any run; 48 complete runs of v20 (K = 50; also complete runs of v22, X.11), all reported: 39 of 48 succeed, one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson bound 0.6956, so by the plan's rule 0.40 is claimed. B_BUDGET, B_TRUE, X_MAX, A_MAX and S2CAP never acted in R7 (largest attempt 197,334 work units, at most 310 stage-2 pairs, true B' cost at most 2^28.60 units); CCAP and A_ADV acted only as the algorithm prescribes. R5 and R6 ran v19's K = 96; they are history (W.8), not pooled with R7.

Executed evidence (not the claimed cost): R7 (proof W.2, Appendix F) with the collisions of its first 15 successful runs as certificates; r5-R-0..7 re-derive 16 seed-picked R7 successes per review; r5-bpfull runs a whole B' of an R7 run from its label, checks R7's table and bound and runs connector attempts with organizer coins; r5-count checks v22's counted stage 1 and its block price (X.4), T2 leaf and state step (X.2), P's core-by-core driver on a sub-problem and its cap (W.4) and P's certifying level on the output core; r5-mitm-0, 1 check seed-picked cores, v22's half-vector step (X.3), per_a and match step with its unrolled run loop (X.1); r5-trail-0..3 recount T1, T2 and the half vectors.

heuristics.statement: Averaged over all of the algorithm's own coins (B' candidate coins, connector coins), the probability p that v22's algorithm (v20's, X.11) outputs a collision satisfies p >= 0.40. Premise R (run selection and coins): the SHA-256/SHAKE-256 coins of labels fixed before the runs act as fresh coins, and the 48 runs of the pre-registered study R7 are an unselected sample of v20's (equally v22's) runs, so that their success indicators are independent Bernoulli(p) draws. Premise P: P outputs the trail of proof Section 3 within M_CAP.
heuristics.scope: Only the success probability. Each R7 run is a complete run of v20 with label-derived coins (proof W.2): r7run.py makes algorithm()'s calls in algorithm()'s order from r5v20.py, which is v19's experiment file with K_SPACES = 50, A_ADV = 1067, A_MAX = 4268 and S2CAP = 2^11 (and an R5-replay bound written as 96); the shipped r5.py differs from it only in trail_search's loop order (W.4: same output, Lemma W; R7 uses P's certified output, as R5 and R6 did), in the organizer replay tables (W.10) and in the spacing of ten constant tables (AST-checked); v22's r5.py differs from v20's only in the counted programs and their checks (X), which algorithm() never calls, and in whitespace outside algorithm()'s call graph; algorithm() and every definition it reaches are byte-identical to v20's (X.10, X.11). E on a space is fes (exact stage 1, Lemma 4, self-checked at 64 checkpoints) and stage 2 by complete digests in fes's order on at most S2CAP passes, which changes at most which colliding pair of a space is output. In R7, B_BUDGET, B_TRUE, X_MAX, A_MAX and S2CAP never acted: largest attempt 197,334 work units (X_MAX 2^20), stage-2 counts 199-310 (S2CAP 2^11), true B' cost at most 2^28.60 units (B_TRUE 2^29), at most 1,201 attempts in a run (A_MAX 4268); CCAP and A_ADV acted only as the algorithm prescribes (per-run table, W.2). Premise P concerns success only: every cost term of P is a fixed count, an organizer-recomputed count or a cap. Output correctness and every cost cap hold without H1.
heuristics.extrapolation: R7: 39 of 48 runs succeed; under premise R the one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson bound is 0.6956, so by R7's pre-registered rule the claim 0.40 is supported. Premise R: rule K, R7's plan, driver, analysis, launcher, experiment file and enumerator were hashed at 2026-10-08T15:23:01Z before any run and made read-only; every run is reported (proof W.2, Appendix F: per-run table and ledger with result-file hashes); the plan's only outcome-dependent rule is whether to claim; which runs the organizer replays and which collisions are certificates was fixed before any result existed. The model that chose K predicts p_50 = 0.739; R7 measures the algorithm itself. Premise P: P's native run certifies the trail by Lemma P; it agrees with v14's exhaustive T3 passes; the organizer re-runs the output core's certifying level, seed-picked cores and P's core-by-core driver on a sub-problem. Organizer checks of R7: r5-R-0..7 re-derive 16 seed-picked R7 successes per review from their labels; r5-bpfull re-runs a whole B' of an R7 run; the first 15 R7 collisions are certificates.
heuristics.limitations: Label-seeded SHAKE-256 coins stand in for fresh words (premise R). R7's failures, run order and timing are logged by us. The organizer re-derives 16 of R7's 39 successes per review (run 22 only in the per-run ledger); failures are not re-run. Rule K was written after G2, C, D, C', R5 and R6 had run, with their outcomes known (proof W.1); R7 ran after rule K and its plan were hashed. R5 and R6 (K = 96) are not runs of v20. P's full-scale certification rests on our native run (296 CPU-s, reproducible from Appendix A); the organizer checks 3 of 467 cores per review at the certifying level.

heuristics.statement: The charged development - v14's G2 (2^30.9572 units; its B' runs at true cost and its E spaces at v22's counted E), v15's D15 at the counted prices of v22's programs (2^32.0018 units, the native T3 runs with their half vectors at every level and the T1/T2 run behind cores.bin), v17's D16 (2^27, bound), our D19 (2^28.8303), our D20 (2^29.0748), v21's D21 (2^22.6078, its build checks of the routines whose ideas v22 adopts) and our D22 (2^26.7962, every run we made for v22 except executions of the organizer's harness) - contains every target-specific run whose result fixed, or under its plan could have changed, a number that v22's algorithm reads, and these prices are the ones the cost model requires. K, A_ADV, A_MAX and S2CAP come from rule K, an a-priori analysis hashed before the evidence run R7, so v14's pre-registration C (whose only role was keeping K = 96) fixes no number of v22. X_MAX and B_TRUE come from v13's run-free rule. Every other run produced program text, verified logged results, measured success under a pre-registered plan whose only outcome-dependent decision is whether its package is claimed (R5, R6, R7; for R7 the alternative was v19, a separate package, not another constant: W.3), re-derived logged computations (v17's B' re-derivations, V.5; executions of the organizer's harness, W.10, X.10) or fixed no number (A1: proof V.6).
heuristics.scope: Only the development (preprocessing) part of the time and preprocessing claims. The algorithm's own terms (2^30.4623) are caps, fixed counts and recomputed counts at counted prices or stated bounds, and do not depend on H2.
heuristics.extrapolation: Proof 0.1, U.5, W.3, W.6 and X.8 list every run (v15's list, D16, the B' re-derivations of V.5, every run made for v19, v20 and v22, with hashes). Rule K's inputs are exact facts of P's output and R7's design; its full history is in rule.txt itself and in W.1. D15 at v22's prices is computed only from v15's published itemization (V.3) with the match and key prices changed, the half vectors of the native runs priced at every level (W.5) and U.4's T1/T2 run added. G2's B' runs were re-derived from their labels by v17 and are priced at their true cost (V.5); its E spaces at v22's counted block (X.4, X.5). D20 and D22 are itemised in W.6 and X.8 at counted prices. Sensitivities: C charged 33.6128; C, R5 and R6 charged 35.3218; R7 charged 33.9770; all four 35.5610; our local organizer runs charged 33.3294; D22 doubled 33.1117; D21 not charged 33.0924; no repricing at all 33.1571.
heuristics.limitations: Rule K was written after C, R5 and R6 had run, by an author who knew their outcomes; it counts as a priori only because it reads none of them and was hashed before R7 (W.1); a reader who rejects that premise should use the sensitivities above. Repricing development at the submitted programs' prices is the rule of v14, v15 and v17, applied again in v22 (X.5); v22's gain over v20 rests on it: a reader who rejects it should use 33.1571 (no repricing of G2, D15, D19, D20; above v20's 33.14493). A1 (v7's design study, 10,432 CPU-s) stays uncharged as in v13-v20; charged 40.9861. v17's B' re-derivations charged 33.9101. R7's plan would have fallen back to v19 on failure; a reader who charges R7 for that gets the R7 sensitivity above (W.3). D15's largest item is an upper bound (the stopped run is charged complete); D15 doubled 33.6485. D16 is v17's stated bound. B2's re-count, which would fix a number of the claim, was not run (X.7).
